'''''Veronica dabneyi''''', the '''Azores speedwell''', is a [[flowering plant]] species of the family [[Plantaginaceae]], [[endemic]] to the [[Azores]]. It inhabits very humid rocky slopes, and also close to waterfalls and lake margins, at altitudes between {{convert|200|and|600|m|abbr=on}}. It is present only in the [[Western Group]] of islands ([[Corvo Island|Corvo]] and [[Flores Island (Azores)|Flores]]).<ref>{{cite web |title=Veronica dabneyi Hochst. |url=https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/5B6NG |publisher=[[Catalogue of Life]] |access-date=31 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Veronica dabneyi Hochst. |url=https://acores.flora-on.pt/#/1veronica+dabneyi |publisher=[[Flora-On]] |access-date=31 March 2021}}</ref> It was thought to be extinct as it had not been observed since 1938, but was rediscovered in 1999, making it a [[Lazarus taxon]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pereira |first1=J. C. |last2=Schäfer |first2=H. |last3=Paiva |first3=J. |title=New records of Veronica dabneyi Hochst. (Scrophulariaceae), an Azorean endemic plant not collected since 1938 |journal=Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society |date=2002 |volume=139 |issue=3 |pages=311–315 |doi=10.1046/j.1095-8339.2002.00060.x |language=en |issn=1095-8339|doi-access=free }}</ref>
